quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: When braking on slippery surfaces, you should apply the brakes:

options.text: Quickly.
Later than usual.
More abruptly than usual.
Earlier than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Earlier than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces like snow or ice, apply your brakes slowly and steadily. Start braking earlier than you normally would. This gives your vehicle more time to slow down safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
Roadwork or maintenance is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roadwork or maintenance is present.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs warn you about construction or maintenance work ahead. They help keep drivers and pedestrians safe in these areas. Fines for traffic violations may be doubled in these zones.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see you better, even if they don't help you see much further ahead.

questions.question: When you see this road sign, you should:

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a divided highway is starting. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.
Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the left and right sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: At these locations, always look left and right to check for anything entering your path. This includes pedestrians, other vehicles, or trains.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting angry, you should:

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Distance yourself from the situation.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, avoid eye contact and hand gestures. Slow down or move away to put distance between you and them. Do whatever you can to stay safe.

questions.question: You want to turn right at the next intersection. You should signal:

options.text: At least 50 feet before the turn.
When you reach the intersection.
At least 100 feet before the turn.
As soon as you see cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 100 feet before the turn.
questions.explanation: You must signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Use your turn signals or hand signals.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination faster.
Follow closer to other cars.
Stay farther away from other cars.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from other cars.
questions.explanation: In wet weather, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop safely.

questions.question: Pressing the brakes hard on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels and causes you to lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels and causes you to lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on ice and snow can lock your front wheels. When this happens, you lose control of steering. Slow down before you reach icy areas so you don't need to brake hard.

questions.question: At a stop sign with a crosswalk but no stop line, you must stop:

options.text: Before the crosswalk.
50 feet before the intersection.
Where you think the stop line would be.
With your front wheels in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, stop before the stop line if there is one. If there is no stop line, stop before you enter the crosswalk. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before you enter the intersection.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if you have to drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if there is an available passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use your cruise control.
Change speed and direction more slowly than normal.
Drive the same way you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction more slowly than normal.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, change speed and direction slowly. Do not use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance from other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always obey speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What line allows you to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 miles per hour, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make unsafe moves to pass you.

questions.question: What should you worry about most when you see this sign?

options.text: Your headlights will be out of alignment because one side of your car is higher.
You could damage a tire if you drift onto the shoulder.
You could hydroplane if water is on the shoulder.
You could lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You could lose control if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the shoulder is lower than the road. If one wheel drops onto the low shoulder, do not slam the brakes or turn sharply. This can cause you to lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When parked parallel to the curb, when can you get out on the traffic side?

options.text: During daytime when other drivers can see you.
When the traffic light turns red.
When you will not interfere with oncoming vehicles.
If you use your four-way flashers first.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will not interfere with oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: After parking, do not open your door if it will interfere with bikes or other traffic. Always check for traffic before exiting your vehicle.

questions.question: After passing a car, when can you return to the right lane?

options.text: When you see the front bumper of the other car in your rearview mirror.
After you use your turn signal.
After you turn your headlights on.
When the other car's headlights turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the front bumper of the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, look in your rearview mirror to see the front bumper of the car you passed. Look over your right shoulder to make sure there is space between your vehicle and the other car. Then you can return to the right lane.

questions.question: A five-ounce glass of wine has the same amount of alcohol as:

options.text: One pint of whiskey.
One 12-ounce can of beer.
A gallon of wine.
A six-pack of beer.

questions.correctAnswerText: One 12-ounce can of beer.
questions.explanation: A five-ounce glass of wine, a 12-ounce can of beer, and 1.5 ounces of whiskey all contain about the same amount of alcohol. All three will impair your driving ability equally.
